tower-of-hanoi.title: Output move list as final answer
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After constructing the solution, explicitly output the move list in the required [[disk, from_peg, to_peg], ...] format as the final part of the response.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When the solution is ready, place the move list at the very end of the response, after any brief reasoning.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Providing only reasoning without the move list, or placing the move list before other text.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Free blocked larger disks by moving top smaller disks first
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the disk you need to move is not on top of its peg, first relocate the smaller disks that sit above it to another peg, respecting all rules.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to move a disk that is not the topmost on its source peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Trying to move disk 4 while disk 2 is on top of it, without first moving disk 2.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Consolidate all disks onto a single source peg before applying classic Hanoi recursion
tower-of-hanoi.principle: When the initial configuration is split across multiple pegs, first move the smaller disks onto a single auxiliary peg so that the remaining larger disks are all on one peg; then apply the classic recursive Hanoi algorithm.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When the start state has disks on more than one peg and you want to use the standard Hanoi recursion.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Applying the classic recursion directly while disks are scattered across pegs, leading to illegal moves.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate destination peg before each move
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before committing a move, ensure the destination peg is either empty or its topmost disk is larger than the moving disk; otherwise the move would violate the size rule.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Every time you propose a move, check the destination peg's top disk.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 4 onto a peg where disk 2 is on top, which is illegal.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Keep answer concise and place move list at the very end
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Generate the move list directly after any brief reasoning and do not add any extra text after it, so the parser extracts the correct list.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When formatting the final response, after any reasoning output only the move list and nothing else.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Adding extra commentary after the move list, causing the parser to miss the final list.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate source peg before each move
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before moving a disk, ensure that the disk is the topmost disk on its source peg; if it is blocked by smaller disks, move those smaller disks elsewhere first.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Every time you propose a move, check that the source peg's top disk matches the disk you intend to move.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move disk 2 from a peg where disk 1 is on top.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may stop after reasoning without generating the required move list.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always include a move list; even for trivial cases, output at least an empty list [] if no moves are needed.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Truncated move list (incomplete solution) due to token limit
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model runs out of tokens or stops early, leaving the move list incomplete.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Plan a concise solution that fits within token limits, and ensure the final move list is complete before ending the response.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a non‑top disk (source peg top mismatch)
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model forgets to check the source peg's top before issuing a move, especially when focusing on freeing larger disks.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always verify that the source peg's top disk is the one you intend to move; if not, relocate the blocking smaller disks first.
